topic: Vertebrate Groups: Fishes, Amphibians, Reptiles, Birds and Mammals
title: Frog vs Lizard vs Crow vs Cat Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A frog on the hostel steps, a lizard on the wall, a crow on the wire and a cat under the bicycle stand. All four have a backbone, yet each belongs to a different class. Diya asks what exactly makes a frog different from a lizard. The answer is in their skin, their heart and how they keep warm.

You will see the vertebrates split by jaws (Agnatha and Gnathostomata), then into Pisces and Tetrapoda, and meet every NCERT class with a labelled diagram: Chondrichthyes (Scoliodon), Osteichthyes (Labeo), Amphibia (Rana), Reptilia (Calotes), Aves (Corvus) and Mammalia (Felis). An animated heart shows blood moving through two, three and four chambers, then cold blooded vs warm blooded, a shark vs rohu comparison with a pause and think check, a worked example that places the four hostel animals, the exam trap about the air bladder, an original NEET pattern match-the-following question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 37 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 A frog, a lizard, a crow and a cat
0:32 The splits: jaws, then fins or limbs
1:02 Every class, one labelled diagram at a time
2:05 The heart: two, three and four chambers
2:45 Shark vs rohu + pause and think
3:33 Worked example: place the four hostel animals
3:58 Exam trap: does the air bladder help a fish breathe?
4:17 Practice question (NEET pattern)
4:42 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Distinguishing Features and Representative Examples. A whale that is not a fish, and a bat that is not a bird.
